_schema_notes.coverage: Authoritative schema for all DID formats — DD Form 1664 (pre-2014) and free-text (post-2014 MIL-STD-963C)
_schema_notes.did_format: Set to 'dd_form_1664' or 'free_text'. Determines which fields are expected to be populated.
_schema_notes.963c_compliant: True if the DID was prepared under MIL-STD-963C (2014 or later). False for older DIDs.
_schema_notes.reserved_fields: Fields marked RESERVED are present in one format but not the other. Always include them — set to empty string or empty array when not applicable.
_schema_notes.preparation_instructions: Official MIL-STD-963C name for what was previously called 'requirements'. Contains the numbered sections of the DID. All section numbers are normalized to strictly numeric dot-notation (1, 1.1, 1.1.1). Letter-based source numbering (2.a, 3.1.b) is converted to numeric equivalents (2.1, 3.1.2).
_schema_notes.asterisk: True if the requirement number is followed by * in the source document (conditional requirement).

title: Dynamic Object Oriented Requirements System (DOORS) Package
summary: Defines the format, content, and use of the DOORS Database package for documenting requirements management compliance and bidirectional traceability, including subcontractor-developed requirement documents, across all DoD acquisition program phases.
use_relationship:
This Data Item Description shall be used in preparing all ongoing, interim, or final Dynamic Object Oriented Requirements System (DOORS) Database modules. The purpose of these modules is to present compliance of requirements management and bidirectional traceability, to include management of all subcontractor-developed requirement documents.
This DID contains the format, content, and intended use information for the DOORS package. It is intended that all requirements contained herein shall apply to all applicable DoD acquisition programs through all program phases.
distribution_statement: DISTRIBUTION STATEMENT A: Approved for public release; distribution is unlimited.

preparation_instructions.title: Reference documents.
preparation_instructions.content: The applicable issue of the documents cited herein, including their approval dates and dates of any applicable amendments, notices, and revisions, shall be as cited in ASSIST at the time of the solicitation; or, for non-ASSIST documents, as stated herein.

children.title: MDA Directive 5000.15, "Ballistic Missile Defense System requirements Traceability Process,"
children.content: [current version via Missile Defense Agency (MDA) Portal or Secretary General Staff Action Control Office (MDA_SACO@MDA.MIL)] as government furnished information (GFI). This Ballistic Missile Defense System (BMDS) Requirements Traceability Handbook provides detailed process for implementing and administering processes for BMDS requirements traceability within routine systems engineering and program technical reviews.

children.content: [current version via MDA Portal or MDA Secretary General Staff Action Control Office (MDA_SACO@MDA.MIL)] as GFI. The MDA System Verification Plan describes the trace process and verification sequence by rollup requirements.

children.content: [current version via MDA Portal or MDA Secretary General Staff Action Control Office (MDA_SACO@MDA.MIL)] as GFI. The memorandum provides an organizational chart of the requirements/specification hierarchy.

children.title: MIL-STD-961, "Department of Defense Standard Practice - Defense and Program-Unique Specifications Format and Content,"
children.content: available at https://assist.dla.mil. The MIL-STD-961 provides requirements for the preparation of defense specifications and program-unique specifications prepared either by DoD activities or by contractors for the DoD.

children.title: The DOORS Database shall be provided in the following formats:
The respective DOORS Package Contract Data Requirements List (CDRL) shall specify versions as an additional requirement.
Format 2 defines the Trace Certification Memorandum (TCM)
Format 3 defines the Prime Item Description Specification (PIDS)
*.PDF file from Adobe and IAW MIL-STD-961.
Format 4 defines the Requirements Traceability Verification Metrix (RTVM)
In contractor format and machine-readable by the Government.
DOORS Database shall consist of the following:
TCM
children.content: is a certification of Element Requirements Trace as defined in DOORS Partition and shall contain:

children.title: PIDS
children.content: Format and content of performance specification shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraphs 4.1 through 5.14

children.title: PIDS Sheet
children.content: Format and content of performance specification sheets shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraphs 5.16 through 5.16.4

children.title: PIDS Revision
children.content: Format and content of performance specification revisions shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraphs 5.17 through 5.17.2

children.title: PIDS Supplement
children.content: Format and content of performance specification supplements shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraphs 5.15 through 5.15.9

children.title: PIDS Amendment
children.content: Format and content of performance specification amendments shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraphs 5.18 through 5.18.7

children.title: PIDS Inactive for New Design Notice
children.content: Format and content of inactive for new design notices shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraph 5.19.2

children.title: PIDS Cancellation Notice
children.content: Format and content of cancellation notices shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraph 5.19.3

children.title: PIDS Reinstatement Notice
children.content: Format and content of reinstatement notices shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraph 5.19.4

children.title: PIDS Reactivation Notice
children.content: Format and content of reactivation notices shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraph 5.19.5

children.title: PIDS Administrative Notice
children.content: Format and content of administrative notices shall be IAW MIL-STD-961, paragraph 5.19.6

children.title: Cover Page and Documentation
children.content: The RTVM software database files shall contain the following:

children.title: Cover Page
children.content: Enter the Title, Date of Issue, Revision Date Contract Number, Contractor's name and address, Distribution Statement (as delineated in the contract), Export Control Warning Label (as delineated in the contract and if applicable), and Security classification.

children.title: Record of Change Page
children.content: Enter a record of all changes made to the RTVM.

children.title: Database Architecture Description Pages
children.content: Enter a detailed description of the database, show relationships and define all the terms, acronyms used in the database fields.

children.title: Data Description
children.content: Describes the data to be contained in the RTVM relational database.

children.title: Unique Identification Number (UID)
children.content: Enter the UID for every requirement in the system configuration baseline (functional and physical).

children.title: Source document
children.content: For each specification and source document, enter the document number and title for the source of each requirement statement.

children.title: Specification or Source Document Paragraph Number
children.content: Enter the specification or source document paragraph number for each requirement.

children.title: Requirement Text
children.content: Enter the specification or source document requirement text.

children.title: Requirement Traceability
children.content: For each requirement, identify and show the traces between all other requirements for within specification tree layers and the system configuration items.

children.title: Requirement Type
children.content: The RTVM database shall identify if the requirement is derived or decomposed from a parent requirement.

children.title: Requirement Attribute
children.content: For each requirement define whether the requirement is a measure of performance, design parameter, software functional requirement, interface requirement, physical parameter, core standard, environmental and cybersecurity (This data field can encompass other data attributes if needed.)

children.title: Requirement Status
children.content: Identify the Requirement status for each requirement, as approved, under review. The status shall identify the latest revision number.

children.title: Non-Conforming Requirements
children.content: For non-conforming requirements, enter the System Trouble Report (STR) and/or Deficiency Report (DR) number and title.

children.title: Hyperlink
children.content: Provide hyper-link to the STR and DR databases.

children.title: Design Reference
children.content: Enter the specific piece of design information (i.e., design document section, drawing, etc.) associated with each requirement.

children.title: Requirement Allocation
children.content: Enter the specific system, subsystem, hardware item, component, Computer Software Configuration Item, Computer Software Component and Computer Software Unit that each requirement has been allocated. System level (e.g., Element Specification) requirements shall be allocated to all Configuration Items defined for the system.

children.title: Form of End Product
children.content: Enter the form and maturity level of the end product used for verification. For example the form can be the system, subsystem, unit level, software configuration Item and the maturity level can be the first article, production representative, prototype or final configuration item.

children.title: Verification Method
children.content: For each requirement, enter the verification method as follows IAW MIL-STD-961, Section 4-Verification (5.9):

children.title: Analysis
children.content: An element of verification that uses established technical or mathematical models or simulations, algorithms, charts, graphs, circuit diagrams, or other scientific principles and procedures to provide objective evidence that states requirements are met.

children.title: Demonstration
children.content: An element of verification that involves the actual operation of an item to provide objective evidence that the required functions were accomplished under specific scenarios. The items shall be instrumented and performance monitored.

children.title: Examination
children.content: An element of verification that is generally nondestructive and typically includes the use of sight, hearing, smell, touch, and taste; simple physical manipulation; and mechanical and electrical gauging and measurement.

children.title: Test
children.content: An element of verification in which scientific principles and procedures are applied to determine the properties or functional capabilities of items.

children.title: Verification Document
children.content: Enter the document number, title, and date of the verification document that contains the verification method.

children.title: Verification Document Paragraph
children.content: Enter the verification document paragraph number that provides the verification method.

children.title: Verification Procedure
children.content: Enter the verification procedure section, and verification procedure step(s) that provides the verification method for each requirement.

children.title: Other Tests
children.content: Enter the names of other tests conducted, prior to verification of the requirements, where the requirements are tested.

children.title: Verification Results
children.content: Enter the results of the verification for each requirement. Did system under test conform to the requirement? (Yes, No).

children.title: Corrective Actions
children.content: Enter all corrective actions taken and the results of the corrective actions.

children.title: Comments
children.content: Enter explanatory notes as required.

children.title: Specification Tree shall illustrate the documentation of decomposition flowing from the Government source requirements down to the PIDS and Component Specifications.
Top Level
children.content: Government Source (System Specification (SS), Element Specification (ES), Interface Control Document(s) (i.e., System Interface Control Document (SICD), Interface Control Document (ICD), etc.), Facilities Requirements Document (FRD), etc) traced to PIDS and/or Element Specification.

children.title: Second Level
children.content: Critical Components (i.e., SRS, SDD, HRS, HDD, etc.) traced from Top Level and PIDS.

children.title: Lowest Level
children.content: Component Specification (if applicable, for each major component and can be separate tree from higher levels) traced from previous level(s).
